items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-08-01
items.q: I can remember making record collectors sit down and listen to Johnny Byerstoffer's band... I'll tell you, that was, Byerstoffer was, I think they only got about four sides out of... And I still think those were two of the best sides out of New Orleans in the 20s that I'd

ctx.x: You were marvelous then. I mean, it went to that extreme with some people. Yeah. I'm sure it depended on who said it. Yes, and people. Well, I can remember playing with the music, and I was like, I'm sure it was a little bit of a little bit of a little bit of a little bit of a little bit of a little bit of colorless to colorless to colorless to colorless to colorless to colorless to colorless to colorless to colorless to colorless to colorless to colorless to colorless to colorless to colorless to colorless to…
I'll tell you, that was, Byerstoffer was, I think they only got about four sides out of, two sides? Two. And I still think those were two of the best sides out of New Orleans in the 20s that I'd
ever run across. I always regretted that I never interviewed him, I knew him. Was he? Oh. And he came back, do you remember? No, I don't. He even played at the famous store for a little while.
